newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures close sharply higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures close sharply higher in thin trade.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Monday's Tokyo session sharply higher, but the rise was exaggerated by thin volume, traders said.
The December closed 0.62 higher at 125.32, its high for the day.
"Volume was thin in both cash and futures. There was no particular news that drove prices higher, only dealers' short-covering," said a trader at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
The volume of the December contract was 38,638 contracts.

"There were some players who had created shorts on the expectation that the December would face resistance at a level slightly below 125.00, which is a half-way retracement from recent lows. These positions were apparently squeezed out," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
"Until the release of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) tankan report next week, the market should continue to be dominated by dealers' position-adjustment activities amid thin volume," the first trader said.
The BOJ will release it key short-term survey of corporate sentiment, known as the "tankan", on November 27.
The March contract also ended sharply higher at 124.36, up 0.65, on rollover from the December contract, traders said.
The March is expected to take over the benchmark position from the December before the end of this month.
Some small-lot buying by investors was detected in cash JGBs, amid thin volume, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.570 percent, down from 2.625 percent on Friday.
In addition to the tankan, market participants were cautious ahead of the 10-year JGB auction expected sometime next week, traders said.
"As there are big events due next week, players are generally reluctant to move this week," said a trader at a Japanese brokerage house.
